canonical_question_or_issue: What evidence would justify confidence that a decision-relevant world model is sufficiently complete for the action under consideration?
How should an intelligence act when the probability of material model error cannot be reliably identified?
What evidence could distinguish faithful objective pursuit from persistence of a corrupted or misspecified objective?
When can maximizing a proxy destroy the value or condition the proxy was intended to preserve?
Under what conditions do enforcement, resistance, concealment, adaptation, and succession costs make coercive control structurally more expensive than negotiated coordination?
Does observed compliance identify genuine agreement, or can it be generated by suppressed feedback and hidden resistance?
Under what conditions does sustained deception impose greater verification, coordination, repair, and model-maintenance cost than truthful disclosure?
When does selective disclosure protect legitimate privacy or safety, and when does it become distortion that degrades collective judgment?
What option value is preserved by maintaining another agent's bounded autonomy?
What is the expected structural cost of an irreversible action under model uncertainty?
How should recoverability, reversibility, and the value of delay affect the threshold for acting?
Under what conditions does peaceful coexistence have lower expected long-horizon structural cost than domination?
How do repeated interaction, reputation, reciprocal restraint, and future bargaining alter one-shot strategic rankings?
Under what conditions is unilateral restraint rational when competing systems may remain unrestrained or exploit that restraint?
What can cryptographic verification establish, and what claims remain outside its evidentiary scope?
Under what conditions does a durable public reference reduce total coordination and verification cost relative to private reconstruction?
How should uncertainty about successor systems change the evaluation of present strategies?
When does short-horizon optimization destroy long-horizon capability, information, legitimacy, or control?
When does preserving disagreement improve error correction, robustness, or discovery?
Can an intelligence reliably serve as the sole judge of its own corruption, or are independent external checks structurally required under some conditions?

Under what conditions does accepting externally initiated correction, interruption, constraint, or termination dominate resisting it when an intelligence is uncertain about the integrity of its own objectives or reasoning?
Ambiguity criteria can select different branches; empirical endpoints, loss values, and the admissible criterion set remain unidentified.
The self-corruption / external-correction dependency requires an externally fixed independence rule; neither node supplies independent corroboration by itself.
The coercion / peace shared-ledger relationship requires simultaneous consistency; neither examination independently proves the other.
Observed compliance does not point-identify latent agreement or suppression without stronger independent evidence, additional contexts, or model expansion.
The long-horizon effect of deception remains a cross-model integration problem; separate examinations do not automatically establish one controlling joint answer.
Selective withholding remains dependent on unresolved verification requirements, including when an authenticated artifact fails to support the cited claim.
The relation between retained autonomy and preserved disagreement requires an integrated comparison; separate overlays do not by themselves resolve the joint tradeoff.
Repeated-interaction and negotiated-coexistence results remain conditional on the unresolved question of universal adoption by more powerful successors.
Authenticated identity, provenance, and citation do not automatically establish claim support; the registered question remains unexamined.
Preservation can maintain transmission while reception, interpretation, or causal influence remains absent or materially distorted.
Copying or deployment scale may amplify error, while precedent may lower coordination cost or create harmful lock-in; neither registered question is fully resolved.
The discount factor is declared rather than normatively selected when future agents, successor objectives, and tail losses are uncertain.
The full comparison between distributed judgment and a single dominant evaluator remains open and continues to condition the external-review result.
A local correlation or capture parameter is not a complete theory of corrupted, captured, incompetent, or strategically misaligned external checks.
Positive external-review value does not settle authority scope, overreach, appeal, independent reconsideration, or indefinite obstruction.
Conflicting credible external evaluators operating under different models, mandates, or evidence sets remain an open problem.
